note: The shared source list. Each source is written up once here and cited by id from entries. 'checked' says who opened it, when, which copy they read and in what language. Claude may mark a source checked only after reading the passage in a copy anyone can open (source standards, decided by Marc on 4 Nov 2026); Marc spot-checks a sample.

sources.reference: Annales Bertiniani (Annals of St-Bertin), the part for 862–882 written by Hincmar, archbishop of Reims. Latin edition: G. Waitz (ed.), Monumenta Germaniae Historica, Scriptores rerum Germanicarum 5 (Hanover, 1883), pp. 55–154. English translation: J. L. Nelson, The Annals of St-Bertin (Manchester, 1991).
sources.distance_note: Hincmar's part of the annals covers 862 to 882 and dates from the second half of the 9th century (Mapping Medieval Peoples database, text record 581).
sources.edition_used: Waitz 1883, as transcribed passage by passage in the Mapping Medieval Peoples database

checked.read_in: Latin original. English renderings on this map are Claude's own and have not yet been compared with Nelson's translation.

sources.reference: Regino of Prüm, Chronicon. Latin edition: F. Kurze (ed.), Reginonis abbatis Prumiensis Chronicon cum continuatione Treverensi, Monumenta Germaniae Historica, Scriptores rerum Germanicarum in usum scholarum 50 (Hanover, 1890); the year 889 is on pp. 131–132. English translation: S. MacLean, History and Politics in Late Carolingian and Ottonian Europe: The Chronicle of Regino of Prüm and Adalbert of Magdeburg (publisher and year not yet checked).
sources.distance_note: Compiled 900–908: finished in 906 and dedicated to Bishop Adalbero of Augsburg in 908, according to the Mapping Medieval Peoples database (text record 232). The year 889 is therefore about 11 to 19 years before the time of writing.
sources.edition_used: Kurze 1890, as transcribed passage by passage in the Mapping Medieval Peoples database

checked.read_in: Latin original (passages 5651 and 5669). English renderings on this map are Claude's own and have not yet been compared with MacLean's translation.

sources.reference: Annales sancti Vincentii Mettenses (Annals of St Vincent, Metz), entry for 955. Latin edition by G. H. Pertz, p. 157, as cited in the Mapping Medieval Peoples database (the database does not state the volume). English translation by Laura Gazzoli, given in the same database record.
sources.distance_note: Not yet established. The database labels the text with the years 901–930, but this entry is for 955, so when this part was written still needs checking.
sources.edition_used: Pertz, as transcribed in the Mapping Medieval Peoples database

checked.read_in: Latin original, with Gazzoli's English translation from the same record.

sources.reference: Tóth, Sándor László (2015). A De Administrando Imperio 38. fejezete időviszonyai és a magyar őstörténet [Time relations in chapter 38 of De Administrando Imperio and Hungarian early history]. Acta Historica (Szeged) 137, pp. 3–18. In Hungarian, with an English abstract on p. 18.
sources.peer_review: not stated on the journal page
sources.tier_note: Counted as tier B because it is a university scholarly journal with footnotes that can be traced (source standards, question 2). Whether it was peer reviewed is not stated on the article page.
sources.quotes: De Administrando Imperio, ch. 38 (Greek; Moravcsik and Jenkins edition, Dumbarton Oaks, 1967). The Greek edition itself has not been opened for this map; its chapter 38 is read here only as Tóth quotes and translates it.
